title: 20 km/h. A completed simulation record.
summary: The corrected fixed-hull run reaches 1.57998 seconds, with 24,342 force samples and four new flow checkpoints. A stronger numerical baseline for the next stage of development.
heroAlt: Computed underside hull pressure at the final saved time of 1.579983709 seconds
heroCaption: 20 km/h boundary-speed target · final saved checkpoint · fixed hull. Total pressure includes the hydrostatic contribution; display range −3,000 to +6,000 Pa.

sections.title: A completed milestone
sections.text: The corrected run completed normally with exit code zero at an actual simulated time of 1.579983709 s—within one final timestep of the 1.58 s target. The combined record contains 24,342 force samples with no duplicate timestamps. It covers approximately 5.014 nominal hull flow-through times, including the initial 0–0.20 s speed ramp. This establishes a completed numerical commissioning record.

sections.title: What the extended record shows
sections.text: Over 0.95–1.579983709 s, the time-weighted mean drag is 80.40 N, mean vertical force is 156.39 N, and mean bow-up pitch moment is 194.65 N·m. Their fluctuation RMS values are 8.12 N, 32.49 N and 23.10 N·m respectively. These are provisional fixed-hull commissioning statistics—not a measured board-performance rating. Vertical force includes buoyancy.

sections.title: Keep the complete force history visible
sections.text: The traces below retain the original samples from both run segments, including the startup transient. The dashed line marks the continuation from 0.95 s. Drag is −Fx, vertical force is Fz, and bow-up pitch moment is −My. No smoothing has been applied; the oscillations are part of the evidence.

sections.title: Check more than one averaging window
sections.text: All four windows end at the final saved time, with starts at 0.95, 1.10, 1.25 and 1.40 s. Mean drag ranges from 80.40 to 81.88 N; mean pitch moment ranges from 194.65 to 197.87 N·m. Their aggregate means are approximately stationary, while a converged periodic distribution has not been demonstrated. Mean vertical force falls from 156.39 to 151.60 N as the window narrows, and fitted slopes reverse sign. It remains drifting and window-dependent.

sections.title: Inspect the final water surface
sections.text: This is the actual saved alpha.water = 0.5 interface at the final checkpoint. Colour represents elevation using a fixed −0.10 to +0.10 m range. Projected surfaces may overlap and out-of-range values saturate. The fields support qualitative inspection of the evolving near-hull flow and wake; they are not yet a settled or experimentally validated wake prediction.

sections.title: Follow the saved sequence
sections.text: The three earlier checkpoints below lead into the final view above. All use the same projection, extent and colour range so changes can be compared directly. These are saved solver surfaces, not interpolated or generated waves.

sections.title: Read the flow in three planes
sections.text: The centre plane at Y = 0 shows the longitudinal flow; the waterline plane at Z = −0.01 m shows flow around the hull; the wake plane at X = −0.25 m provides a transverse view behind it. Each uses velocity magnitude from 0 to 8 m/s at the same final checkpoint. These slices include air and water, rather than water-only velocity.

sections.title: A traceable numerical result
sections.text: The full corrected run recorded a maximum Courant number of 0.3204 and maximum interface Courant number of 0.2979. None of the force signals was classified as numerically unstable. The completion audit confirms 156 protected case/checkpoint hashes and three CAD/STL source hashes. Original force histories remain byte-for-byte consistent with the preserved 0.95 s record. The open-domain water inventory changed by +0.0190%; this is not by itself a conservation residual, because integrated phase flux balance was not evaluated.

sections.title: What comes next
sections.text: The report recommends retaining the current geometry. Load and wake stationarity, mesh sensitivity and experimental validation remain the next evidence needed before selecting a geometry change or claiming final performance. A fixed hull cannot establish running trim or equilibrium, and the mean vertical-force-to-weight ratio is not a payload or support rating. The completed run gives those next investigations a documented baseline.

sections.title: Keep the earlier milestone in context
sections.text: The original 0.95 s commissioning record remains available as the preceding stage. The present article carries the completed extension, updated force statistics and later saved fields.
